items.title: Ed Allen Interview, 1961-01-14
items.q: And I played them with Clarence, he liked that. So if I play something else, he scored.

ctx.x: Did anybody teach it to you? No. Each one have an individual style, you know. You play something that sounds good. And I played them with Clarence, he liked that. So if I play something else, he scored. I used to play some sweet melody with me playing, Clarence. Come on, cuz. They don't want to hear that. Give me some quack, quack, quack, quack. You like that, man. Come on, quack, quack. That ain't like listening to that. That ain't you. Play some quack, quack, quack, quack. I used to get some quack, quack,…
had the comedy said it was too sweet? Yeah.
